covert

/KOH-vert/ - the stress falls on KOH · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Covert means carried out in secret.

The recall was covert by agreement: mechanics fixed the flaw during routine oil changes, and no notice was ever mailed to owners.

Worked Example

For eight months the museum ran a covert loan check, sending interns posing as tourists to inspect its traveling paintings in other cities — no gallery on the route was told.

Covert is stronger than discreet or private. A private matter is simply not shared, and a discreet one is kept quietly in the background — a covert operation is actively disguised, built so that even people looking straight at it cannot tell it is happening.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

stealthy: Stealthy describes the manner of moving — soft-footed, quiet, slipping past notice in the moment, like a cat crossing a dark yard. Covert describes the design of a whole undertaking: a covert operation is built so that nobody can tell it exists at all.

hush-hush: Hush-hush is the playful, informal word for secrecy kept by simply not talking about a thing — a hush-hush engagement, a hush-hush deal. Covert is sterner and more active: a covert program is deliberately disguised, dressed as something else so that onlookers cannot recognize what is happening.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

aboveboard: done in full view, with nothing to hide

public: open to everyone's knowledge

Where it sits · how actively the thing is hidden — private → discreet → covert

private vs. covert: Private is far milder than covert — a private matter is simply not shared, and nobody has to disguise anything to keep it so.

discreet vs. covert: Discreet stops short of covert: a discreet inquiry stays quietly in the background, while a covert one wears a disguise so that even onlookers cannot tell it exists.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — cover-

Root — cover-: to hide from view (Old French covrir)

Suffix — -t

Suffix — -t: old French past-participle ending: 'covered'

Put it together

Put it together: Covert is Old French for 'covered' — covrir, 'to cover,' wearing its old participle ending -t. A covert operation is literally an operation under cover. Its opposite number is overt, from Old French for 'opened': overt acts happen in the open, covert ones under the lid.

Use the root in a new word: undercover
